newsitem.title: USA: Iowa soybean harvest wrapping up, corn still wet.
newsitem.headline: Iowa soybean harvest wrapping up, corn still wet.

text.p: Iowa farmers were wrapping up soybean harvest in the week ended Sunday but corn remained too wet to harvest, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
Soybeans were 83 percent harvested as of Sunday, against 86 percent average. Corn harvest was 17 percent complete, compared with 39 percent for the five-year average.

"The moisture level of corn remaining in the field averaged 27 percent, while the moisture level of harvested corn averaged 23 percent," the report said. Last year at this time, corn in the field averaged 20 percent moisture.
Corn lodging was rated mostly none to limited with 36 percent rated none, 48 percent light, 15 percent moderate and one percent heavy.
Winter wheat was 80 percent seeded as of Sunday, in line with the five-year average but behind last year's pace.
Soil moisture was rated six percent very short, 27 percent short, 65 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
Pasture and range condition rated three percent very poor, 20 percent poor, 31 percent fair, 39 percent good and seven percent excellent.
